sentences.text: ORAL ORDER Order in First Appeal No.4609 of 2007 1.

This appeal is filed under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act by the Oriental Insurance Company assailing the judgement and award dated 13.07.2006 in MACP No.775 of 1997, passed by the Claim Tribunal, Ahmedabad (Rural).

Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd vs Jivatben Wd/O. Bhikhaji Dahyaji Tahkor on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123156365/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant Insurance Company, being aggrieved by the award of compensation, has preferred the present appeal, inter alia, alleging that the amount awarded is on higher side.
The background facts are that on 17.04.1997 the deceased Bhikhaji Thakor being occupant of camel cart sustained fatal injuries when the camel cart dashed with the opposite vehicle TATA 609.

The respondents claimants being widow and sons and daughter had filed a claim petition under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation against driver, owner and insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4609/2007 ORDER DATED: 16/10/2023 undefined company of the offending vehicle.

The learned Claim Tribunal after considering the evidence on record, had considered Rs.4,000/- as monthly income and applying multiple of 15 awarded a sum of amount Rs.4,80,000/-
under dependency benefit.

3. The appellant insurance company has preferred the present appeal for reduction of the amount mainly on the ground that the monthly income of Rs.4000/- assessed is on a higher side and,
therefore, the Tribunal in a fact situation ought to have assessed Rs.2000/-.
4. This Court has heard learned counsel Mr.C.J.Vin and Rushang Mehta for the respective parties.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of the material placed on record, the issue falls for my consideration is as to whether the award of compensation is excessive and requires reduction.
6.
The answer of the issue is in negative.
The reasons are that before the Tribunal the widow as well as witness Mansi Jhala Exh.52, Bababhai Kolhi Exh.53 have categorically stated about the multipurpose activities undertaken by the deceased.
The deceased was agriculturist and revenue record Exhs.25 and 28 supported the version of the witnesses on the issue of income.
The learned Tribunal has believed the income of Rs.3000/- of the deceased from agricultural operations and Rs.1000/- from the milk business.
It is to be noted that the learned Tribunal without considering the future income, straightway awarded the amount under the dependency benefit.
So if the Tribunal would have considered the future prospects then award will rise further.

Thus, therefore,
non- consideration of the future prospective income by the Tribunal, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4609/2007 ORDER DATED: 16/10/2023 undefined monthly income assessed Rs.4000/- is just and reasonable so as to reach a reasonable amount of compensation.
7. For the reasons stated, the present appeal is devoid of any merits and is hereby failed and dismissed.
Decree be drawn accordingly.
Order in Civil Application (for stay) No.3 of 2007 in First Appeal No.4609 of 2007
In view of the order passed in First Appeal, civil application does not survive.
Disposed of accordingly.
